interface.name: infinity_window_manager_v1

description.summary: private window geometry channel for malaysia-shell

interface.description:
This protocol is private to malaysia-shell. It lets the shell ask the compositor to place windows in halves, quarters, pairs and fullscreen arrangements, and reports the D-Bus addresses of each window's global menu.
The shell identifies windows with the same zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 objects it already uses for the dock. Requests are silently ignored when the handle no longer names a tracked window.

request.name: arrange

description.summary: place one window in a layout

request.name: arrange_pair

description.summary: tile the active and previous windows as a pair

request.description: The active window takes the first half and the previous visible window in focus order takes the second half.

description.summary: tile the four most recent visible windows in quarters

request.name: restore

description.summary: restore the window to its pre-arrange rectangle

request.description: Applies the rectangle saved by the first arrange and clears it.

request.name: set_fullscreen
request.description: A non-zero value enters fullscreen covering the whole output; zero leaves it and restores the previous rectangle.

request.name: force_quit

description.summary: kill the process that owns a window

request.description: The compositor sends SIGKILL to the client process behind the window, as macOS Force Quit does: a hung app ignores a polite close, so the shell asks for this only after the user confirms. Every window of that process goes away. The compositor never kills itself.

event.name: restorable

description.summary: whether the window has a stored restore rectangle

event.description: Sent whenever the stored rectangle changes so the shell can enable or disable the restore action.

event.name: app_menu

description.summary: D-Bus address of the window's global menu

event.description:
The com.canonical.dbusmenu service and object path of this window's menu, as announced by the client over org_kde_kwin_appmenu. Empty service and path mean the window has no menu.
Sent when the address changes, when the toplevel handle is created and when the manager binds, never when focus changes.

event.name: gtk_menus

description.summary: D-Bus address of the window's GTK menu

event.description:
The D-Bus bus name and object paths exported by a GTK 3/4 application for its global menubar and app menu. Empty values mean the window has no GTK global menu.
Sent when the address changes, when the toplevel handle is created and when the manager binds, never when focus changes.

enum.name: focus_bar

description.summary: the bar over the shown space

enum.description: Whether the shown space is a focus space and, if so, whether the bar is down over it (the pointer at the top edge).

entry.name: none
entry.summary: a desktop is shown; the bar is the usual one

entry.name: hidden
entry.summary: a focus space is shown and the bar is up

entry.name: revealed
entry.summary: a focus space is shown and the bar is down

event.name: space
event.description:
The row of spaces (Malaysia ADR 0051): which one is shown, how many there are, the shown desktop's number as the user sees it («Escritorio 3»), 0 for a focus space, and the bar's state over a focus space. Over a focus space the bar is drawn in absolute black with white text.
Sent when the manager binds and whenever any value changes.

arg.name: count
arg.summary: how many spaces the row has

arg.name: desktop
arg.summary: 1-based desktop number, 0 for a focus space

request.name: send_shortcut

description.summary: type a keyboard shortcut into a window

request.description: The compositor focuses the window and types the chord into it, as if the user pressed it, bypassing compositor shortcuts. It backs the shell's shortcut menus for apps that publish no global menu. keys is modifiers then one xkbcommon keysym name joined with '+', for example "Ctrl+Shift+S". The request is ignored when a key is unknown, the session is locked or the window cannot take keyboard focus.
